Header: Streptomyces scabiei scab; scab of potato

Prevention: Plant disease-free seed tubers i.e. clean certified tubers.
Avoid applying fertilizers and other material (ash, lime, poultry manure) that make the soil alkaline just before planting as this will encourage the disease development especially in region 3 of
Avoid planting in fields that had diseased crops such as tomato, eggplant, Irish potatoes, and carrots.
Maintain high soil moisture for 2-3 weeks by regular irrigation (4-5 days intervals) in early stages after tubers form (about 3 weeks after sowing).
This closes the soil surface and reduces the penetration of the disease to the tubers.
Clearing crop debris that were affected in previous harvests and alternate hosts such as tomato, carrots and eggplants near the field.
Incorporate cabbage and mustard residues into the soil to suppress the development of the disease.
Monitoring: Common scab is caused by a soil and tuber borne bacterium.
Check some tubers during the tuber formation stage for scab spots which are circular, brown, roughened areas, with irregular margins that are sunken or raised.
The spots are corky (differentiates it from powdery scab lesions).
Check for surface lesions and discoloration on the stems.
When you find symptoms on several plants in your field, consider direct control actions.
Direct Control: Ensure tools are disinfected after use to avoid contamination and spread to other areas.
Test the pH of the soil using a laboratory service, this will allow you to use the right type and amount of acid forming nitrogen fertilizer to regulate the soil pH.
Restrictions: There is no chemical control available for the common scab disease on potatoes at present
